solutions.latex: Sketch $y=\cos x$ and $y=|x|$: they intersect twice. Answer B.
$f(x) = g(3x) = \sqrt{3x-6}$. Answer C.
$|k| = 3$ and the graph is flipped, so $k=-3$. Period $T = 4\pi = \dfrac{2\pi}{a}$, so $a = \dfrac{1}{2}$. $c = \dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2} = 1$. Answer C.
$x \in [-3, 3]$, so $y \in [1, 2\times 3 + 1]$, i.e. $y \in [1, 7]$. Answer A.

Amplitude $= |-3| = 3$.

Period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/4} = 2\pi \times \dfrac{4}{\pi} = 8$.

$x \in [-\pi, \pi]$, so $2x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]$ (2 revolutions).

$\tan 2x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Positive revolution: Q1: $2x = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$; Q3: $2x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$.

Negative revolution: Q1: $2x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} - 2\pi = -\dfrac{11\pi}{6}$; Q3: $2x = \dfrac{7\pi}{6} - 2\pi = -\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

$\therefore x = \dfrac{\pi}{12}, \dfrac{7\pi}{12}, -\dfrac{11\pi}{12}, -\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$
$\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, and at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0$. So $\tan x = \dfrac{1}{0}$ is undefined (it cannot be reached), hence $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is an asymptote.

$0 = 2 - 4\cos t$, so $\cos t = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Q1: $t = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Q4: $t = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.

$\therefore t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$

Maximum $v$ occurs when $\cos t = -1$: $v = 2 - 4(-1) = 6$ m/s.

The particle reaches a maximum velocity of $6$ m/s at $t = \pi$ seconds.
\exfigure{461_q9_s1}

Method 1: $\dfrac{2x-5}{x-3} = \dfrac{a}{x-3} + b = \dfrac{a + b(x-3)}{x-3}$, so $a - 3b = -5$ and $b = 2$. Then $a = -5 + 6 = 1$, so $\dfrac{2x-5}{x-3} = \dfrac{1}{x-3} + 2$.

Method 2: $\dfrac{1}{x-3} + 2 = \dfrac{1 + 2(x-3)}{x-3} = \dfrac{2x-5}{x-3}$, so LHS = RHS.

Vertical asymptote $x = 3$, horizontal asymptote $y = 2$. $y$-intercept: $\dfrac{5}{3}$. $x$-intercept: $\dfrac{5}{2}$. Also $(4, 3)$ lies on the curve.

\exfigure{461_q10_s1}
$x \in (-\infty, 3)$

Horizontal: translate 3 left: $3 \to 3 - 3 = 0$.

Vertical: reflect, then up 2: $8 \to 8\times(-1) + 2 = -6$.

$\therefore (3, 8)$ is transformed to $(0, -6)$ on $g(x)$. Check: $g(0) = -6$.
The parabola must be moved up by more than 16 so there are no $x$-intercepts, so $k > 16$.

The asymptote of $f(x)$ has moved down by 1, so $c = -1$.

$f(1) = a\times 2^1 + c = 0$, so $a = -\dfrac{c}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\therefore a = \dfrac{1}{2},\ c = -1$

1st: vertical dilation by scale factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$ (from the $x$-axis), giving $h(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}f(x)$.

2nd: horizontal dilation by scale factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$ (from the $y$-axis), giving $k(x) = h(2x) = \dfrac{1}{3}f(2x)$.

3rd: horizontal translation 1 unit to the right, giving $g(x) = k(x-1) = \dfrac{1}{3}f(2(x-1)) = \dfrac{1}{3}f(2x-2)$.

The sketch passes through $(-0.5, -2)$, $(1.5, 0)$ and $(3.5, 2)$.
